items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: that left an opening for me to join Tommy Dorsey in 1947... I stayed with him for three years

ctx.x: Did you give him like a week’s notice this time when you left?

Yeah, I gave him proper notice this time, yeah. I played it straight this time. And after that, Benny was kind of semi-retired then. He was going to go back to New York and not do too much, so that left an opening for me to join Tommy Dorsey in 1947. And that was a great experience, a wonderful band. He had people in there like Charlie Shavers the great trumpet player, Ziggy Elman was still in the band then, Paul Smith on piano, and Tommy himself was just superb you know. I stayed with him for three years, and…

of us said “we have a chance to join Duke Ellington’s band.” So he looked at us and hesitated for about fifteen seconds, then he said “take me with you.” I’ll never forget those words you know. But he was a great man. Harry was a great player and a sensational band besides you know. But I did get a chance to work with him for a while. And then of course after that, of course with Ellington, there are so many stories about that band, and Ellington himself was an element of surprise, always. Because you never knew…

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s when I joined Tommy Dorsey’s band.

ctx.x: We’re getting a little ahead of ourselves if you’re already talking about being with the Goodman band, so let’s back up. You’re still in high school. You’re studying. You’ve been studying with Roy Knapp. How long did you study with Roy?

With Roy Knapp? I studied with him for about three years. I gained a lot of knowledge, and it gave me a chance to go to Chicago, take my lesson from him, then stay over a day or two, and like I said before, go to catch Cab Calloway, Gene Krupa, Tommy Dorsey, Duke, Basie. I caught all of them.

The biography in The New Grove Dictionary of Jazz lists that you learned tap- dancing, or were a tap-dancer with a barrelhouse pianist, Speckled Red. You said that you played with him. Did you also – is that an accurate account? Were you also a tap dancer?

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then from ’55 to ’56 you were back with the Dorsey brothers? ... That band had – Charlie Shavers was in that band. ... We did a whole season of shows.

ctx.x: There’s another example of Duke Ellington reversing it: jazz – zajj. That’s another one of those.
Then from ’55 to ’56 you were back with the Dorsey brothers? How did that come about?
